title: Data collection without legal basis
description: Child's GPS location data may be collected without proper legal basis or consent, especially problematic for children's data under COPPA/GDPR-K
assumptions: Assumes data collection occurs without explicit parental consent or legal authorization

title: Lack of notice about data collection
description: Child may not be adequately informed that their live GPS coordinates are being transmitted to the backend
assumptions: Assumes minimal or no notice is provided to the child about data collection

title: Data used for undisclosed purposes
description: GPS location data may be used for purposes not disclosed to the child or parent, such as tracking beyond intended scope
assumptions: Assumes data collection purpose is not fully transparent to the data subject

title: Inaccurate GPS data quality
description: Live GPS coordinates may be inaccurate, delayed, or contain errors affecting the reliability of the data
assumptions: Assumes GPS signal quality varies and may not always be accurate

title: Location data stored without proper consent
description: Location pings are written to the Location History Store without explicit user consent or appropriate consent management mechanisms.
assumptions: Assumes location data collection is part of the app's core functionality

title: Location data disclosed to unauthorized parties
description: Location history stored in DS1 may be accessed by unauthorized parties through data breaches, insider threats, or system vulnerabilities.
assumptions: Assumes DS1 is accessible to multiple system components

title: Location data accidentally deleted or corrupted
description: Location pings written to DS1 may be accidentally deleted, corrupted, or lost during storage operations.
assumptions: Assumes standard data storage operations without redundancy

title: Unauthorized access to location history
description: The Location History Store may be accessed by unauthorized users or systems, leading to exposure of sensitive location information.
assumptions: Assumes DS1 has appropriate access controls

title: Non-compliance with privacy regulations
description: Storing location pings may violate privacy regulations such as GDPR, CCPA, or other data protection laws requiring specific consent and handling procedures.
assumptions: Assumes jurisdiction-specific privacy regulations apply

title: Excessive location data transmission
description: Mobile App Backend may forward all location pings to Geofencing Engine without filtering or limiting to only necessary location data for geofencing zone checks, potentially transmitting more data than required.
assumptions: System forwards all incoming location pings without applying data minimization filters.

title: Inaccurate location data forwarding
description: Location pings forwarded from Mobile App Backend to Geofencing Engine may contain inaccurate or incomplete location information due to GPS errors, network location inaccuracies, or timing issues, potentially leading to incorrect geofencing alerts.
assumptions: Location data quality depends on device GPS/network accuracy and timing synchronization.

title: Lack of legal basis for location processing
description: Processing of location pings for geofencing may lack a clear legal basis or lawful justification, especially if users have not provided explicit consent for location tracking.
assumptions: Legal basis for processing must be established before location data is forwarded.

title: Location data used for individual identification
description: Geofencing Engine may use location data to uniquely identify individuals, potentially enabling tracking of user movement patterns and behavior across different geofencing zones.
assumptions: Location data can be correlated with user identity and used to track individual movement.

title: Potential non-compliance with privacy regulations
description: Geofencing processing of location data may not comply with applicable privacy regulations (e.g., GDPR, CCPA) regarding location data processing, consent requirements, and data subject rights.
assumptions: Privacy regulations impose specific requirements for location data processing.

title: Location data exposure in zone definitions
description: Zone definitions (home, school, friend's house) contain sensitive location information about family members that could be exposed if the data store is compromised or accessed by unauthorized parties.

title: Unauthorized disclosure of family location data
description: Family account zone definitions could be disclosed to unauthorized third parties through data store breaches, API misconfigurations, or insider threats.

title: Inaccurate or outdated zone definitions
description: Zone definitions may become outdated (e.g., school address changes, moved homes) leading to incorrect geofencing behavior and potential privacy violations.

title: Accidental deletion of zone definitions
description: Zone definitions could be accidentally deleted or corrupted during processing, potentially causing loss of critical family location tracking data.

title: Unauthorized location tracking
description: The geofencing engine may track and record location-based events (zone entry/exit) without explicit consent from individuals, potentially violating privacy expectations around location data.
assumptions: Assumes the system collects location data from individuals entering/exiting defined zones.

title: Inappropriate disclosure of location information
description: Location-based notifications sent to the parent external entity may disclose sensitive information about individuals' movements and whereabouts without adequate consent or transparency.
assumptions: Assumes the parent entity may have access to this location data.

title: Unique identification through movement patterns
description: The geofencing notifications may enable identification of individuals based on their unique movement patterns and zone access history, potentially leading to profiling.
assumptions: Assumes movement patterns can be used to identify individuals uniquely.

title: Non-compliance with data protection regulations
description: The sharing of location-based notifications may not comply with applicable data protection regulations (e.g., GDPR, CCPA) regarding consent, purpose limitation, and data minimization.
assumptions: Assumes the system operates under applicable data protection laws.

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Child's Personal Information
description: Child's sensitive profile data (name, DOB, school, geofence zones) could be disclosed to unauthorized parties during registration, storage, or processing by the mobile app backend.

title: Potential Lack of Legal Basis for Data Collection
description: Data collection for child profiles may not have adequate legal basis or proper consent mechanisms, especially for minors under age 13 (COPPA) or 16 (GDPR-K).

title: Potential Non-Compliance with Child Privacy Regulations
description: Data flow may violate child-specific privacy regulations (COPPA, GDPR-K) regarding collection, processing, and storage of children's personal information.

title: Unintended Consequences from Geofence Zone Data
description: Geofence zone definitions could lead to unintended location tracking, surveillance, or profiling of the child beyond intended purposes.

title: Inaccurate or Incomplete Child Profile Data
description: Child's profile information (name, DOB, school) may be entered incorrectly or incompletely, affecting data quality and potentially leading to identification errors.

title: Insufficient Notification of Data Collection Purposes
description: Parents may not be adequately informed about how child data will be used, stored, and shared, reducing transparency and informed consent.

title: Lawful basis for collecting child profile data
description: Backend collects child profile data without clear legal basis or appropriate consent mechanism, particularly concerning for minors' personal information.

title: Integrity of child profile data
description: Risk that child profile data could be tampered with, corrupted, or modified without authorization, potentially affecting location-based restrictions.

title: Excessive geofence zone data collection
description: System may collect more geofence zone data than necessary for the stated purpose, violating data minimization principles.

title: Accuracy of geofence zone data
description: Geofence zone data may be inaccurate or outdated, leading to incorrect location-based restrictions or access controls.

title: Unauthorized use of stored account data
description: Stored account and child profile data may be used for purposes beyond the original intended family account management purpose.

title: Data availability for family account access
description: Risk that stored account and child profile data becomes unavailable when needed, potentially blocking legitimate family member access.

title: Excessive location data collection
description: Parent may request more location data than necessary for the stated purpose, including historical location data that could be used for tracking or profiling beyond the immediate need.
assumptions: Parent may not fully understand the extent of location data being collected.

title: Location data can uniquely identify child
description: Location data, especially when combined with other data, can be used to uniquely identify the child and potentially track their movements over time.
assumptions: Location data is collected with sufficient granularity and frequency to enable identification.

title: Lack of notice about location data usage
description: Parent may not be adequately informed about how location data will be stored, shared, or used beyond the immediate viewing purpose.
assumptions: Notice mechanisms may be insufficient or unclear.

title: Location data may be inaccurate or incomplete
description: Location data provided may be inaccurate, delayed, or incomplete, affecting the parent's ability to make informed decisions about the child's whereabouts.
assumptions: Mobile app backend may not ensure data accuracy or completeness.

title: Potential legal basis concerns for location data processing
description: Processing of location data, especially for minors, may raise legal concerns regarding consent and legal basis for data processing.
assumptions: Legal framework for location data processing may not be fully established.

title: Potential regulatory non-compliance with location data laws
description: Mobile app backend may not be fully compliant with applicable regulations (e.g., GDPR, COPPA) regarding collection and processing of location data, especially for minors.
assumptions: Regulatory requirements for location data may not be fully implemented.

title: Unauthorized access to location history data during retrieval
description: Location history data stored in DS1 could be accessed by unauthorized parties during the retrieval process to P1, potentially exposing sensitive location information without proper authentication or authorization controls.

title: Location data accessed without user consent
description: Location history data may be retrieved from DS1 to P1 without explicit user consent or awareness, violating user privacy expectations and potentially breaching consent-based privacy frameworks.

title: Location data used for purposes beyond intended use
description: Location history retrieved by P1 may be used for purposes other than serving the map/history view, such as user profiling, advertising, or tracking, without user knowledge or consent.

title: Location history data integrity compromised during storage
description: Location history data stored in DS1 could be tampered with, corrupted, or altered before retrieval, potentially leading to inaccurate or misleading location information being served to users.

title: Excessive location data retrieved beyond necessity
description: P1 may retrieve more location history data from DS1 than is necessary to serve the map/history view functionality, violating data minimization principles.

title: Unauthorized secondary guardian access to child location
description: Secondary guardian may not be who they claim to be, or authentication mechanisms may be weak, allowing unauthorized individuals to access the child's location data.

title: Excessive location data sharing with secondary guardian
description: Location data shared with secondary guardian may exceed what is necessary for the intended purpose, potentially exposing more child location information than required.

title: Insufficient notice about data sharing with secondary guardian
description: Parent may not be fully informed about what data is being shared, with whom, and for how long, potentially violating transparency requirements.

title: Inaccurate or outdated location data for child
description: Location data may be inaccurate, delayed, or outdated, potentially leading to incorrect decisions about child safety or supervision.

title: Unauthorized Legitimacy for Location Sharing
description: The mobile app backend may grant access to secondary guardians without proper verification of their legitimate relationship to the child, potentially allowing unauthorized individuals to access sensitive location data.
assumptions: Assumes the system relies on user-provided guardian information without robust verification mechanisms.

title: Inadequate Notice to Child/Parent
description: The child or parent may not be adequately informed about the extent and duration of location data sharing with the secondary guardian, violating transparency requirements.
assumptions: Assumes notice mechanisms exist but may not be clear or comprehensive.

title: Excessive Location Data Minimization
description: The backend may share more location data than necessary (e.g., continuous tracking vs. periodic updates), violating data minimization principles.
assumptions: Assumes the system shares location data continuously rather than on-demand or at intervals.

title: Improper Usage of Location Data by Guardian
description: The secondary guardian may use the child's live location data for purposes beyond the intended scope (e.g., surveillance, tracking beyond parental boundaries).
assumptions: Assumes guardians may have access to the data and could misuse it.

title: Non-compliance with Privacy Regulations
description: The data flow may not comply with applicable privacy laws and regulations regarding sharing of minors' location data with third parties.
assumptions: Assumes various privacy regulations exist that may not be fully considered.

title: User behavior data can be linked to individuals
description: Aggregated usage and engagement analytics may contain patterns that can be correlated with other data sources to identify individual users, even if intended to be anonymized
assumptions: Assumes the advertising partner has access to other user data or the analytics can be correlated with other datasets

title: User behavior data disclosed to unauthorized parties
description: Analytics data shared with advertising partner could be accessed by unauthorized parties, leaked, or shared with third parties beyond the intended advertising partner
assumptions: Assumes the advertising partner has appropriate security controls and access restrictions

title: User data used in unintended ways
description: Analytics data could be used for purposes other than funding the free tier, such as targeted advertising, data resale, or profiling beyond the stated purpose
assumptions: Assumes the advertising partner has clear terms of service and adheres to them

title: Data sharing violates privacy regulations
description: Sharing user analytics may violate GDPR, CCPA, or other privacy regulations if consent is not obtained or if data handling practices do not comply with applicable laws
assumptions: Assumes the app has obtained user consent for data sharing and implemented appropriate privacy controls

title: Excessive location data collection for check-in
description: Child sends current location for routine check-in which may not be necessary for the intended purpose. Location data should be minimized to only what is essential for the specific use case.

title: Unintended access to location data during transmission
description: Location data transmitted from child to parent could be intercepted by unauthorized parties during network transmission, potentially exposing sensitive location information.

title: Inaccurate or outdated location information
description: Child may provide inaccurate, outdated, or spoofed location data, compromising the reliability of the check-in/SOS message and potentially leading to incorrect parent awareness of child's whereabouts.

title: Insufficient notice about location data sharing
description: Child may not be fully informed about how their location data will be stored, used, and shared with third parties beyond the parent process.

title: Potential lack of legal basis for location data processing
description: Processing of child's location data may lack clear legal basis or adequate consent, particularly if data is retained beyond the immediate SOS/check-in purpose.
